page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying AMD EPYC processor features a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, cryptography acceleration, and virtualization.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling and memory subsystem performance are more constrained. Multi-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with uncached read and write speeds registering at 37.53 GB/sec and 15.4 GB/sec respectively, placing the PassMark memory score in the bottom 10%. Text processing and single-threaded compression tasks perform at average levels, while database operations, static web serving, and medium-sized LLM inference tasks show weaker performance profiles.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the c3d-highcpu-4 offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints or local storage. The instance is best suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale software compilation. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases, high-throughput web serving, or multi-threaded parallel computing due to its constrained memory bandwidth and multi-core scaling limitations.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. It operates with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, backed by a 32 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core CPU execution, placing in the top 25% for single-core stress tests, though multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth are comparatively weak. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server provides a resource-dense configuration for compute-focused tasks. It is best suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight utility scripting, text processing, and basic web serving where high memory capacity is not required.
